detailed_description: The JSON Viewer helps you paste JSON text, parse it in the browser, and inspect the result as a collapsible tree. It starts with a sample JSON object and shows parsing errors when the input is not valid JSON. After parsing, nested objects and arrays can be expanded or collapsed one node at a time, or expanded and collapsed together with the toolbar buttons. This makes it useful for quickly checking the structure of API responses, configuration snippets, or copied JSON payloads without editing the original data.
usage_steps: Paste JSON text into the input area or edit the sample JSON already shown
Click Parse & View to parse the text in the browser
If the JSON is invalid, read the parsing error shown below the buttons
Explore the parsed tree by expanding or collapsing nested objects and arrays
Use Expand All or Collapse All when you want to open or reset the whole parsed tree
usage_examples: A web developer pastes an API response to inspect nested objects and arrays in a tree view.
A frontend developer checks a JSON configuration snippet before copying it into a project.
A support engineer pastes a JSON payload from a log and expands only the relevant branches.
A data analyst quickly confirms whether copied JSON text parses before using it elsewhere.
